title: Expert ownership, compact slots, and runtime route partition

sources.notes: Authoritative immutable owner table, all built-in policies, indexed targets, per-target dense slots, optional resident-byte capacity checks, sparse bank coverage, manifest schemas, environment policy parser, and CPU opt-in. The Reyu model executes policy algebra on a bounded ten-expert row; apportionTwoRemote is a rational two-card counterpart to the source's float-based largest-remainder calculation. Serialization bytes, filesystem I/O, and arbitrary card counts are abstract.

Authoritative route-device gather, padding exclusion, disjoint/covering/capable/finite validation, ascending CUDA compact maps, dtype preservation, and zero-weight dummy-slot rule. Tensor payloads are represented as bounded route-position sets; shape/rank and all-remote failures remain explicit.

CPU-focused harness for exact int4 ownership, compaction/dummy slot, geometry, sparse source ids, indexed multi-card policies, unweighted fractional division and capacity rejection. The file also covers admission, allocation and telemetry outside this branch.

Original qualified-35B manifest gate: legacy bank header, all-CUDA/split/interleaved/subset policies, FP8 CUDA forcing, bank coverage, generation, manifest round trip, non-dense slots and unknown policy rejection. It is inventory evidence, not modeled runtime code.

Pins Qwen prefix-bank behavior and Laguna absolute routed layers 1..47 mapping to compact bank rows 0..46. It documents the representational compromise that dense model layer 0 receives CUDA placeholder owners because Placement has no no-routed-row form.

Torch-only synthetic classification harness for split/all-CUDA/interleaved placement, padding, input-weight preservation, invalid coverage/overlap, capable-layer constraints and a valid CUDA/B70/CPU three-way split.

Live all-CUDA versus split:128 token-parity and remote-marker harness. With hybrid enabled but no B70 device, masked remote work is recomputed on CUDA; it exercises partition/merge identity rather than physical B70 transport.

Live eager shadow harness requiring a remote route and checking masked CUDA plus masked remote against full routed output with max_abs < 0.1, cosine > 0.999 and no NaN. Numerical tolerance is documented but not encoded as set ownership.

assumptions: The ten-expert placement domain and five route positions are explicit finite abstractions; production dimensions remain source/configuration inputs.
apportionTwoRemote requires remoteN >= 0 and positive integer weights and models exactly two positional B70 cards; the source validates these preconditions before calling _remote_counts.

apportionTwoRemote uses exact integer rational remainders. It corresponds to the Python source when binary-float proportional shares preserve the same fractional-remainder ordering; extreme integers near a floating tie require direct Python comparison.
The model accepts cudaN as the already-rounded result of Python round(num_experts * cuda_fraction), avoiding a false real-number model of Python ties-to-even binary floating arithmetic.
Each successful build action atomically publishes a complete immutable row, matching build_placement publication rather than exposing mutable construction internals.
denseSlots records the source validator result; the partition model separately exposes remote-to-dummy slot zero behavior but does not enumerate every target slot.
A capable layer is an absolute model layer backed by an offline bank. Capability does not imply that the selected policy makes the layer remotely active.
A Laguna dense-layer CUDA row is a manifest placeholder documented by the topology harness, not a claim that a routed expert module executes in that layer.
Partition mask identity is structural. It does not establish provider success, kernel numerical parity, transport ordering, latency, or final token parity.
Generation replacement occurs only at a caller-controlled coarse boundary; these modules do not implement an online predictive swap protocol.
Only capacities explicitly present in Placement.device_capacities constrain resident expert bytes; unrelated allocations and undiscovered hardware limits are outside validation.
No owned harness, build, test, formatter, linter, GPU workload, or server workload was executed while authoring these artifacts.

implementation_checks.description: CPU differential: compare apportionTwoRemote(5,3,2) with FractionalRemotePolicy((0,1),0.0,(3,2))._remote_counts(5); both should return positional counts (3,2). Also compare the unweighted source branch at remote_n=181 with model weights (1,1), expecting (91,90). Sweep bounded positive weights and report separately any source-float versus rational ordering divergence rather than treating it as model failure.
CPU differential: for 10 experts, cuda_fraction=0.5 and weights (3,2), inspect half-open groups and assert B70:0 owns 0..2, B70:1 owns 3..4, and CUDA owns 5..9, matching weightedLargestRemainderTest.
CPU check: construct explicit two-card groups with independently dense slot-zero origins, round-trip the v2 manifest, then lower one capacity by one byte and confirm overcommit rejection.

CPU check: use remote global ids {0,4,9} and explicit bank_source_expert_ids=(0,4,9), then replace the bank set with (0,1,8); require true then false. Repeat with Laguna absolute bank_layer_ids=1..47 to distinguish it from the prefix fallback.

Torch CPU differential: use global ids [0,3,7,9,-1], a compact map where only 0 and 3 map to local 0 and 1, and finite weights; assert remote/padding ids become dummy zero, corresponding CUDA weights are zero, local entries retain weights, and the output id dtype equals input dtype.

CPU check: build FractionalRemotePolicy((0,1), cuda_fraction=0.0), confirm placement validation succeeds, then confirm dummy-slot validation rejects the all-remote capable rows. This checks the intentional cross-module constraint.

Torch CPU comparison: classify a route row containing CUDA, B70, CPU and -1 padding against a synthetic device-map row, then run validate_partition and compare exact Boolean masks/counts to threeWayPartitionTest.
Torch CPU check: validate matching (max_batch,hidden_size) and (max_batch,top_k) tensors, then supply two mismatched buffers and require one diagnostic containing both observed and expected shapes.
